req.title: Reject limit above cap
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the limit parameter exceeds the maximum allowed.

doc.reasoning: The endpoint GET /tasks/ declares limit with Query(100, ge=1, le=1000). FastAPI/Pydantic will return HTTP 422 for any value > 1000. We need: (1) a positive case confirming a valid limit works (EP), (2) a negative case with a clearly excessive limit (NEG/EP), (3) boundary cases at exactly 1000 (max allowed, must succeed), 1001 (one above cap, must fail with 422), and 0 (below minimum ge=1, must fail with 422). This covers both sides of the le=1000 and ge=1 constraints, catching off-by-one mutations on those constants.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_limit_valid_midrange_returns_200():
    r = client.get('/tasks/?limit=100')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert isinstance(r.json(), list)

test_limit_valid_midrange_returns_200()

tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_limit_far_above_cap_returns_422():
    r = client.get('/tasks/?limit=9999')
    assert r.status_code == 422
    body = r.json()
    assert 'detail' in body
    assert isinstance(body['detail'], list)
    assert len(body['detail']) >= 1

test_limit_far_above_cap_returns_422()

tests.name: test_limit_one_above_cap_1001_returns_422
trace: R-TASK-007 — limit=1001 is one above le=1000; must return 422 (catches 1000->1001 constant mutation)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_limit_one_above_cap_1001_returns_422():
    r = client.get('/tasks/?limit=1001')
    assert r.status_code == 422
    body = r.json()
    assert 'detail' in body
    errors = body['detail']
    assert isinstance(errors, list)
    assert len(errors) >= 1
    assert errors[0]['type'] in ('less_than_equal', 'value_error')

test_limit_one_above_cap_1001_returns_422()
